key_insight: MITE improves biomedical named entity recognition by turning entity extraction into code-like generation across multiple programming languages and combining the predictions by voting.
clinical_relevance: This could make biomedical text mining more robust and accurate for extracting entities from clinical or research text, supporting downstream annotation and information retrieval.
method: Transforms each BioNER example into code-formatted instructions and outputs in Python, C++, and Java.
Trains on multiple language-specific representations to add structural diversity without extra biomedical knowledge.
Uses entity-level voting across formats at inference to reduce prediction variance and improve robustness.
evidence_signal: The approach was evaluated on six widely used BioNER datasets and consistently outperformed representative BERT-based and LLM-based baselines, with cross-dataset generalization reported.
watch_item: The code-formatted setup may add implementation complexity and performance could depend on how well the entity-voting scheme transfers across datasets and languages.
paper_title: Enhancing Biomedical Named Entity Recognition via Multiple Programming Languages Instruction Tuning and Ensemble Method
